name: Fungal Brood Mother
desc: The first major boss. Lurks in a ruined Kin village basement in the Lowlands. Tier 1 — designed to teach players the boss-fighting loop.
appearance: Bloated, slow Kin matriarch overgrown with bioluminescent fungal sacs. Her face is partially preserved, eyes blank but tracking. Trails spore-mist as she moves.
behaviors: Stays mostly stationary, rarely chases.
Spawns 'Spore Mites' (small fast adds) every ~15 seconds.
Telegraphs sac-burst attacks 2 seconds before triggering.
Becomes more aggressive below 30% HP, releases panic spore-cloud.
abilities: Spore-Sac Burst — AOE poison cloud, leaves lingering damage zone
Fungal Spawn — summons 3-5 Spore Mites
Tendril Lash — short-range pull toward her
Death Bloom — final ability, releases all stored spores
drops: Cartographer's Lens (guaranteed — required for first Atlas)

name: Bone Brood Father
desc: A patriarchal corruption in the Badlands. Lives in the ribcage of a colossal Kin elder's skeleton, now half-buried in red sand.
appearance: Skeletal humanoid, almost no flesh, ribs flared like a cage. Skull is enormous, jaw permanently open in a silent howl. Cracked bone armor covers his arms.
behaviors: Slower than Fungal but hits much harder.
Spawns 'Bone Walkers' — skeletal minions that pursue relentlessly.
Uses sand as cover, occasionally burrows briefly.
Will retreat into his ribcage at low HP and channel a final attack.
abilities: Bone Spike Wall — spawns barriers that block player movement
Marrow Lance — long-range bone projectile, high damage
Walker Summon — 4-6 Bone Walkers join the fight
Ossuary Slam — close-range AOE, breaks player armor
drops: Sharp Bone Tip x8 (taxidermy + ammo materials)

name: Frost Brood Lich
desc: Wreathed in perpetual blizzard in the Frozen Peaks. Was once a Kin elder revered for her ice-prophecies.
appearance: Tall, gaunt figure suspended above the ground in a vortex of snow. Crystalline shards float around her like a slow halo. Her eyes are two pinpoints of blue cold.
behaviors: Floats slowly, never touches ground.
Spawns 'Frost Wisps' (fast, fragile, freeze on hit).
Drops temperature in the arena over time — player needs cold protection.
Phases between physical and intangible states.
abilities: Glacial Lance — three-bolt frozen volley
Wisp Tide — summons 6-8 Frost Wisps
Icebound — locks the player in place briefly
Hailstorm — area denial, falling ice shards

name: Aether Brood Empress
desc: Floats serenely above a Sky Island throne. Surrounded by hovering shards of crystal that drift in mathematical patterns.
appearance: Regal Kin form draped in tattered silk. Skin half-replaced with violet aether crystal. Her crown is made of orbiting shards that never touch her head.
behaviors: Highly mobile — teleports short distances around the arena.
Spawns 'Aether Mites' — mini-bosses that mirror her teleport.
Vulnerable only when her crown shards align overhead (3-second window).
Uses gravity attacks — pulls or pushes the player off platforms.
abilities: Crown Shard Volley — fires orbital shards in spiraling arcs
Gravity Reverse — flips up/down briefly
Mite Manifest — 3 Aether Mites appear from rifts
Imperial Decree — temporary invulnerability + summons

name: Vord Brood Queen
desc: Found in an abyssal pit beneath an old Kin temple. Closest creature to the original VORD form. Tier 3.
appearance: No longer recognizably Kin. A wet, segmented mass with multiple eye-clusters and dozens of half-formed limbs. Constantly birthing smaller drones.
behaviors: Stationary — anchored to the pit by her own mass.
Continuous spawn rate of basic Vord Drones (8-12 in arena at all times).
Hits players from across the arena with elongated tendrils.
Below 25% HP, becomes mobile by uprooting from the pit — much more dangerous.
abilities: Tendril Sweep — rotating arena-wide attack
Drone Tide — endless spawn
Acid Spit — long-range ranged attack
Uproot (phase 2) — boss becomes mobile, chases player
drops: Spirit Anchor (rare — Queen partially retains identity)

name: Mech Brood Director
desc: In a Kin ruin that was a pre-corruption automation lab. The Director was a Kin engineer who tried to fight Vord with automation — and lost.
appearance: Half flesh, half scrapped machinery. Spider-like legs, six tool-arms. Face is a brass mask welded to remaining flesh. Eye lenses glow.
behaviors: Constructs minions live during the fight — pulls scrap from the floor.
Has 4 'construction stations' around the arena — destroy them to slow spawns.
Heavy ranged focus — keeps distance.
Repairs itself if left alone for too long.
abilities: Drone Assembly — every 12 seconds, builds a new minion
Servo Strike — long-arm melee from range
Self-Repair — channels for 4 seconds, heals 15% HP
Overload Discharge — AOE pulse from the chest

name: Stone Warden
desc: Tier 1 Warden, guarding a small Lowlands ruin. Slow but devastating melee fight.
appearance: Towering Kin-shaped figure of grey stone, with green moss in the cracks. Wields a massive stone maul. Cracks glow faintly red.
behaviors: Slow movement, telegraphed attacks.
Becomes faster as cracks widen — at 50% HP, charges briefly.
Cannot be staggered by light attacks.
Vulnerable spot: the glowing core in his chest, exposed after a charge.
abilities: Maul Slam — straight-line AOE
Quake Stomp — circular AOE, knocks player back
Boulder Throw — ranged option, dodgeable
Charge Rush — only at lower HP, exposes core after
drops: Stone Cube x12, Iron Ingot x4

name: Iron Sentinel
desc: Guards a Kin smithy in the Badlands. Fully armored, near-invincible from the front.
appearance: Suit of riveted iron plate, three meters tall. The helmet's visor is sealed shut. Sparks bleed from joints when it moves.
behaviors: Cannot be damaged from the front — must hit from behind or sides.
Slow turning, predictable.
Has a 'rage' phase when its armor cracks at 33% HP — much faster and more aggressive.
Stomps create shockwaves that knock back.
abilities: Greatsword Cleave — wide frontal arc
Shoulder Bash — forward charge
Earth Tremor — radial stomp
Rage Phase — strips armor, faster movement, exposed weak points
drops: Iron Ingot x8, Titanium Plate x2

name: Glass Watcher
desc: In a crystalline cave system beneath the Fungal Marshes. Reflective surfaces mean every angle matters.
appearance: Crystalline humanoid with refractive skin that scatters light into rainbows. Cannot be seen clearly from any one angle — always partly invisible.
behaviors: Reflects ranged attacks back at the player.
Must be fought in melee.
Creates 'mirror copies' that look identical — only one is real.
Vulnerable when the cave's natural light hits its core directly.
abilities: Refract — reflects a ranged shot back
Mirror Self — spawns 2 False copies
Crystal Shard Burst — close-range AOE
Prism Beam — laser when caught in direct light

name: Bone Colossus
desc: A multi-skeleton Kin amalgam, fused into one giant. In the Badlands' Bone Reach.
appearance: Massive figure assembled from 5-6 Kin skeletons fused together. Multiple skulls. Multiple arms. Walks on irregular leg combinations.
behaviors: Each skull is a separate weak point — destroy them in sequence to weaken him.
While skulls remain, regenerates over time.
Different arms wield different weapons (hammer, spear, claw).
Final phase: collapses into a single skeleton and becomes much faster.
abilities: Multi-Limb Assault — strikes from several angles at once
Bone Erupt — pillars of bone burst from the ground
Skull Howl — area fear, scrambles player aim briefly
Reassemble — picks up fallen skull bones to regrow
drops: Spirit Anchor (the original Kin who was 'first' in the fusion)

name: Mist Guard
desc: In a Sky Island fortress perpetually shrouded in cloud. Visibility is the central challenge.
appearance: Tall humanoid in a long flowing cloak of mist. Face hidden. Only the gleam of two weapons visible through the fog.
behaviors: Visible only when attacking.
Moves silently through mist when between attacks.
Has a clear 'wind-up' sound before each strike — audio cues critical.
Cleared mist by stunning him with sonic attacks reveals his True position.
abilities: Mist Step — teleports through fog
Twin Cleave — paired blade strikes
Veil Cloak — increases ambient mist density
Gale Step — knocks player off platform edge

name: Void Custodian
desc: Endgame Warden. In the deepest abyss, guarding the path to the Citadel. The most patient fight in the game.
appearance: Tall, robed figure with a featureless mask. Aura of consumed light around it — a sphere of darkness 3 meters wide that swallows projectiles.
behaviors: Projectiles entering its darkness sphere are nullified.
Must be fought in melee or with attacks that pierce the sphere.
Counter-attacks every successful player hit with a precise riposte.
Telegraphs ultimate ability across the entire arena.
abilities: Void Riposte — instant counter on player hit
Darkness Pulse — expands sphere temporarily
Lightless Lance — pierces armor, ignores cover
Final Eclipse — arena-wide darkness for 5 seconds
drops: Spirit Anchor (one of the original Kin Council)

name: Mist Hunter
desc: Tier 1 Hunter. Stalks the Fungal Marshes by night. Fast, low HP, deadly if not tracked.
appearance: Lean Kin figure on all fours, half-corrupted. Skin pale, eyes huge and reflective. Moves silently. Trail of phosphorescent footprints fade quickly.
behaviors: Stays mostly invisible, attacks from behind.
Retreats to recover stealth between strikes.
Can be tracked by faint footprint trail.
Vulnerable in the moment after an attack (1-2 second window).
abilities: Pounce — sudden leap from stealth
Throat Tear — high damage close-range
Mist Veil — re-enters stealth, even mid-fight
Shriek — momentarily blinds player

name: Shadow Stalker
desc: In an old Kin night-watch tower in the Lowlands. Was once a guard captain.
appearance: Long, gangly Kin form draped in tattered dark cloth. Carries two curved blades. Eyes glow faint amber from beneath the hood.
behaviors: Uses environmental shadows to disappear.
Comes from above as often as from the sides.
Reads player's movement — circles to opposite side.
Throws blades from stealth, then closes for finisher.
abilities: Twin Blade Throw — dual ranged attack from stealth
Shadow Step — teleports between dark zones
Finisher Lunge — closes gap from any direction
Smoke Veil — creates shadow zone for cover

name: Spore Hunter
desc: Deep in the Fungal Marshes, a Kin who became one with the spores. Toxic, fast, terrifying.
appearance: Hunched Kin figure overgrown with bioluminescent fungal spores. Trails a constant cloud. Limbs end in claw-spurs of compressed mycelium.
behaviors: Leaves spore zones wherever it walks — visible damage trails.
Faster than other Hunters but more predictable in attack patterns.
Vulnerable to fire damage.
Becomes more aggressive at low HP and stops leaving zones (focused on player).
abilities: Spore Claw — close-range AOE poison
Trail Mark — leaves a damage zone behind
Bloom Burst — circular poison release
Berserker Rush — final phase, ignores zones to chase player

name: Frost Reaver
desc: In the Frozen Peaks, hunting at the treeline. Tier 2. Tracks the player as much as the player tracks it.
appearance: Powerful Kin figure with white-blue skin and frost-rimed eyes. Wears the fur of slaughtered Snowdrifters. Two long ice-bone claws.
behaviors: Stays at edge of player's vision, watching.
Engages only when player commits to an action (drinking, crafting, etc).
Phase 1: hit-and-run. Phase 2: full combat.
Can freeze the player solid briefly with a successful claw hit.
abilities: Hunter's Mark — telegraph attack from far range
Frost Claw — close-range, may freeze
Pack Howl — summons 2 wolves to support
Reaver's Charge — single high-damage commitment

name: Sky Hunter
desc: In a Sky Island spire, hunts from the air. The first fight that meaningfully uses aerial mobility.
appearance: Winged Kin figure — wings are corrupted Driftwing skin grafted to their back. Carries a longbow made of skyserpent bone.
behaviors: Stays airborne almost the entire fight.
Player needs Glider/Gyrocopter or precise long-range to engage.
Lands only briefly to recover quivers.
Vulnerable during its dive-attacks.
abilities: Skyserpent Volley — multi-arrow ranged attack
Dive Strike — committed high-speed dive, exposes weakness on miss
Wing Buffet — knocks player off platforms
Ascend — escapes to higher altitude when threatened

name: Vord Lance
desc: Endgame Hunter. Vord's perfected assassin. The Apostle's chosen.
appearance: Slender, almost beautiful Kin figure. Skin made of black chitin segments. Carries a single spear made of focused void. Moves like liquid.
behaviors: Engages, disengages, repositions — never stays in one spot more than 3 seconds.
Counter-attacks specifically when player misses a swing.
Has a 'final blow' attack at low HP that one-shots — must be dodged perfectly.
Speaks to the player during the fight — old Kin language, half-lucid.
abilities: Void Lance Thrust — high-precision pierce attack
Step-Echo — afterimages confuse player aim
Riposte Reading — counter on missed attacks
Final Verdict — endgame one-shot, telegraphed but hard to dodge
drops: Spirit Anchor (high-value — Lance was a beloved Kin commander)

name: Mire Channeler
desc: Tier 1 Channeler. Lives at the heart of a Fungal Marsh. Turns the arena against the player.
appearance: Stooped Kin figure leaning on a staff topped with a glowing fungal sphere. Robes dripping with marsh water. Long stringy hair.
behaviors: Stays at distance, channels environmental hazards.
Will not approach the player even if attacked in melee.
Vulnerable while channeling (3-second windows).
Surrounding water becomes acidic over time as fight progresses.
abilities: Acid Pool — designates spots that bubble up after 2 seconds
Spore Squall — area cloud damage
Mire Tendrils — grasping vines from below
Channel: Drowning — slows player movement in water

name: Cinder Caster
desc: Badlands volcanic vent. The arena heats up over the course of the fight — player needs heat resistance.
appearance: Tall Kin figure with skin like cracked obsidian glowing orange from within. Robes burn but don't consume. Holds a fistful of molten metal.
behaviors: Arena temperature rises every 30 seconds — player takes burn damage without protection.
Stays mobile to keep distance.
Pyro spirit if cleansed; otherwise turns the arena to lava at low HP.
Vulnerable when channeling Magma Pillar (channels for 4 seconds).
abilities: Molten Volley — three arc projectiles
Cinder Step — leaves fire patches when moving
Magma Pillar — vertical column rises from beneath player
Eruption — final ability, fills arena with lava

name: Frost Conduit
desc: Frozen Peaks, in a crystalline cathedral. Channels are the entire arena — pillars of ice that focus its power.
appearance: Statuesque Kin figure encased in flowing ice, ice flowing upward instead of dripping. Translucent — you can see her heart pulsing.
behaviors: Power is amplified by 4 ice pillars at the arena edges — destroy them to weaken her.
Each pillar destroyed reduces her abilities tier.
Slow movement but constant ranged barrage.
Pillars regenerate slowly — managing them is the fight.
abilities: Glacial Bolt — homing frost projectile
Pillar Resonance — area freeze under ice pillars
Frostfall — overhead ice rain in arena
Heart Beat — pulse AOE that scales with intact pillars

name: Storm Speaker
desc: Sky Island, in a fortress where ancient Kin called the lightning. Wields the storm itself.
appearance: Wild-haired Kin figure standing atop a wind-circled platform. Arms raised, draped in tattered cloth. Eyes are pure white.
behaviors: Calls lightning — strike zones visible 2 seconds in advance.
Manipulates wind to push player away from her.
Has 4 'storm anchors' on the arena floor — break them to disrupt her.
Hardest with metal armor (lightning attraction).
abilities: Lightning Strike — telegraphed AOE
Gale Push — radial wind shove
Static Field — slows and shocks anyone in zone
Cyclone — final phase, central tornado covers half the arena

name: Bone Sigil-Keeper
desc: In a Kin burial complex. Channels through carved sigil-stones placed around the arena.
appearance: Robed Kin priest, skin replaced with carved bone segments. Sigils etched directly into her skull, glowing faintly green.
behaviors: Power flows through 6 sigil-stones at the edges of the arena.
Inscribe each stone takes time — interrupt or destroy them.
Heals when standing near intact sigils.
Becomes more dangerous as stones are removed (desperate phase).
abilities: Sigil Channel — heals herself near stones
Bone Spear Inscription — creates spears from carved sigils
Soul Drain — short-range life-steal
Final Inscription — at 25% HP, etches the player's soul

name: Void Manipulator
desc: Endgame Channeler. In an abyssal void node, manipulates gravity, space, and time.
appearance: Robed Kin figure that flickers between three positions simultaneously. Half-transparent. Eyes are voids — actual voids — that pull light into them.
behaviors: Player gravity reverses unpredictably.
Boss has 3 positions at once — must be hit in all 3 to do real damage.
Time slows in pockets — must read which 'speed bubble' she's in.
Final phase: arena unfolds into non-Euclidean shape, gravity vectors confuse aim.
abilities: Gravity Flip — temporary reversal
Triple Self — exists in 3 places
Time Pocket — slow-motion bubble
Reality Fold — final phase, arena becomes non-Euclidean
drops: Spirit Anchor (an original Kin Council theorist)

name: Tendril Horror
desc: Tier 3 Aberrant. Buried in the foundations of a sunken Kin temple in the Marshes. Reaches through walls.
appearance: No Kin body. Just a central mass of pulsing flesh anchored to the temple's heart-stone, with dozens of long, segmented tendrils extending into the surrounding rooms.
behaviors: Cannot move from its anchor.
Strikes through walls — line-of-sight does not protect.
Tendrils have individual HP — destroying them reduces attack rate.
Phase 2: the anchor lifts, becomes mobile but reduced damage.
abilities: Wall-Pierce Strike — tendril through cover
Sweep — multiple tendrils across a room
Tendril Regeneration — regrows lost limbs over time
Anchor Release — phase change, becomes mobile
drops: Spirit Anchor (the original Kin temple keeper)

name: Echoing Heart
desc: In a vast underground cavern. Fights with copies of itself; the real one is hidden among echoes.
appearance: Floating heart-shaped mass of corrupted flesh, suspended in air. Identical to its echoes — only the player's careful listening reveals which one pulses real.
behaviors: Spawns 4-6 identical decoys at start of fight.
Real heart has a slightly different rhythm — audio cue critical.
Damaging a decoy heals the real one.
Phase 2: respawns decoys, faster cycles.
abilities: Sonic Pulse — area damage from real heart only
Decoy Mirror — spawns copies
Misdirection — swaps positions briefly
Sympathetic Resonance — wrong target damage heals real heart
drops: Spirit Anchor (multiple — the Heart was many people)

name: Hollow Choir
desc: In a Sky Island chapel. Six separate Kin singers must be killed in harmonic order or they heal each other.
appearance: Six Kin figures standing in a circle, mouths open in eternal song. Each robed in a different color. Eyes closed.
behaviors: Six bosses share an HP pool but cannot be killed in any order.
Player must identify the correct harmonic order by listening to each one's voice tone.
Killing wrong order: the remaining heal massively.
Final stage: all six dissonate, become aggressive simultaneously.
abilities: Harmonic Note — individual sonic attack
Dissonance — collective AOE when out of order
Final Chorus — phase 2, all six attack together
Heal Echo — heals when one is killed in wrong order
drops: Spirit Anchor (six separate, all bond as one in the Gateway)

name: Maw of the Abyss
desc: In a deep cave that opens into the void. A gravity well that pulls everything — including the player — toward an event horizon.
appearance: A wide circular pit in the ground. At its center, a slowly-rotating black sphere. Above it, a tentacled mouth-like structure that breathes.
behaviors: Player is constantly pulled toward the central pit.
Falling into the pit is instant death.
Must fight while moving against the pull.
Maw has tentacles that swing across the platform.
abilities: Gravity Pull — constant force toward pit
Tentacle Sweep — wide platform attack
Void Inhale — periodic increase in pull strength
Final Swallow — pit expands, less platform
drops: Spirit Anchor (the Council member who first opened the rift)

name: Forgotten King
desc: Endgame. A corrupted Kin monarch ruling over his own stronghold. Dignified. Lucid. Asks the player to justify themselves before fighting. The moral hinge of Act 3.
appearance: Stately Kin figure on a throne, dressed in well-kept robes. Crown of black metal. Skin partially corrupted but face still recognizably noble. Eyes are sad.
behaviors: Speaks to the player throughout the fight — old Kin language.
Will not attack first; must be provoked.
If player tries to flee, lets them. (Saves quest for later.)
Fights with skill and patience — uses every Warden/Channeler hybrid mechanic.
abilities: Royal Decree — buffs his Vord fodder in the stronghold
Crown Burst — radial holy energy attack
Royal Guard Summon — calls Vord lieutenants
Final Oath — at 1 HP, asks for mercy or final blow
drops: Royal Codex (NPC unlock — Kin Council recipes)
Spirit Anchor (most powerful in the Gateway when freed — speaks the harshest truths)

name: Carapace Apostle
desc: A Kin who chose corruption voluntarily. Worships VORD. Faces the player as a willing servant of the rift.
appearance: Robed figure with chitinous black armor grown over their entire body. Helmet shaped like a beetle's head. Holds a vord-staff carved from rift material.
behaviors: Will negotiate, but only for the player to surrender to VORD willingly.
Fights without remorse — believes they are saving the player.
Has access to multiple Vord abilities simultaneously.
Asks the player at half HP: 'Why do you struggle against peace?'
abilities: Apostle's Conversion — instant kill if player gets too close
Carapace Bash — heavy melee
Vord Ritual — summons abyssal tendrils
Acceptance — at 1 HP, asks player to free them or convert
drops: Spirit Anchor (problematic — Apostle's choice persists in spirit form)

name: The Hollow Source
desc: Act 4 first major fight. Inside the Citadel. A vast Vord creature woven from every type of Kin — smith, beekeeper, dancer, scholar. Cycles through their attack patterns.
appearance: Towering composite figure with multiple Kin bodies fused together. Some hands hold hammers, some hold scrolls, some hold harps. Constantly changing posture as different Kin within take control.
behaviors: Cycles through 6 attack patterns mirroring previous boss families.
Player must recognize the active pattern and respond accordingly.
Each pattern lasts 30-45 seconds.
Fight is genuinely hard — players who skipped archetypes will struggle here.
abilities: Smith Phase — heavy melee like a Warden
Channeler Phase — environmental hazards
Hunter Phase — stealth and pounces
Brood Phase — summons Vord minions
Apostle Phase — wide AOE
Final Cycle — all 6 simultaneously briefly
drops: Spirit Anchor (six in one — the Hollow Source contains all the original Council)

name: The Choice (Variants)
desc: Final encounter, depends on the player's choice at the Choice Chamber. Each ending has its own confrontation.
appearance: The rift itself, or the Apostle, or the player's mirror — depends on the chosen path.
behaviors: Seal — fight the rift itself, as a manifested entity. Reality bends.
Bind — fight the hidden Apostle of the Council, who opposes binding.
Step Through — no fight; an extended traversal sequence into the unknown.
Embrace — fight your own mirror, the Untouched who refused to corrupt.
abilities: Seal path: rift uses every mechanic the game has ever shown
Bind path: Apostle fights with diplomacy mechanics
Step Through path: environmental puzzle, not combat
Embrace path: mirror copies player's exact loadout

name: Vord Drone
desc: The most common corrupted Kin. Rank-and-file of every Vord stronghold. Was once a Kin laborer or farmer.
appearance: Hunched humanoid in tattered work clothes. Skin grey-purple, eyes filmed over. Slow shuffling gait, weak limbs.
behaviors: Slow approach, swings clumsily.
Easily killed individually; dangerous in groups.
No ranged ability.
Tends to clump near the boss for support.
abilities: Clumsy Swing — basic melee
Lunge Bite — short-range attack
Death Spasm — releases small spore puff on death

name: Vord Slinger
desc: Corrupted Kin who once worked as scouts or hunters. Wields a primitive sling or thrown rocks.
appearance: Lankier than Drones, with one arm subtly elongated. Skin grey, eyes dark. Carries a leather sling around their neck.
behaviors: Keeps distance from player.
Hides behind cover between throws.
Fragile in melee — runs if approached.
Often paired with Drones to form a melee+ranged team.
abilities: Stone Sling — ranged attack, moderate damage
Retreat — runs to new cover when approached
Volley — fires three stones quickly when desperate

name: Vord Burrower
desc: Lives beneath the ground in any stronghold. Ambushes players who walk over loose dirt.
appearance: Stocky form, thick arms, no visible eyes — face is sealed flesh with claws around the mouth. Skin nearly the color of dirt.
behaviors: Hides underground until player walks within 3m.
Bursts up for one big attack, then re-burrows.
Telegraphs surface position with rumbling sound and dust.
Cannot follow player onto built grid platforms.
abilities: Surface Strike — emerges with claw attack
Burrow — escapes underground
Drag Down — at low HP, grabs player and pulls into ground briefly

name: Vord Sprinter
desc: Fast, low-HP melee. Was once a Kin runner or messenger.
appearance: Slim, almost graceful corrupted form. Long legs end in pointed feet. Face is mostly intact but eyes are wild and bright.
behaviors: Closes distance to player extremely fast.
Hits once and circles away.
Easy to kill if hit, but hard to hit.
Will not engage in groups — strikes alone.
abilities: Sprint Strike — fast melee on closing
Evade — short hop away after attacking
Frenzy — at low HP, ignores evasion, all-in attack

name: Vord Brute
desc: Heavy mid-tier enemy. Often found guarding important rooms in strongholds.
appearance: Massively muscular corrupted Kin. Skin rough, almost armored. Wears scrap-iron plates wired into the flesh.
behaviors: Slow but deals very high melee damage.
Can stagger players with hits.
Has armor — needs heavier weapons or armor-piercing ammo.
Often guards corruption nodes.
abilities: Heavy Slam — telegraphed AOE
Grab — at close range, picks up player and throws
Armor Shrug — ignores light damage

name: Vord Spore-Bearer
desc: Carrier of fungal corruption. Common in marshes and stronghold interiors.
appearance: Bloated, mushroom-covered humanoid. Cluster of glowing spore-sacs replaces head. Walks unsteadily.
behaviors: Walks slowly toward player, suicide-style.
Explodes in a poison cloud when killed or close to player.
Vulnerable from range only.
Often used as 'pushers' to flush player from cover.
abilities: Death Bloom — releases poison cloud on death
Lurch — slow, inevitable approach

name: Vord Charger
desc: Multi-leg corrupted creature. No longer human-shaped — looks like a Kin that grew extra limbs and lost their face.
appearance: Six-legged horror, body low to the ground. Original Kin torso visible in the center but mutated. Mouth where the head should be.
behaviors: Sprint-charges in straight lines.
Hard to dodge in tight spaces.
Telegraphs charge with screech.
Fragile from sides, armored on front.
abilities: Charge — straight-line high-damage rush
Trample — runs over player after knockdown
Screech — alerts other enemies

name: Vord Climber
desc: Lurks on stronghold walls and ceilings. Drops on players from above.
appearance: Spindly corrupted Kin, all limbs. Hands and feet end in long hooked claws. Eyes on the back of the head — can see in all directions.
behaviors: Stays on walls and ceilings.
Drops onto players from above.
Can be heard skittering before it strikes.
Fragile when on ground.
abilities: Drop Strike — falls onto player from above
Wall Run — moves quickly along vertical surfaces
Claw Slash — close-range attack

name: Vord Shrieker
desc: Non-combat support enemy. Alerts other Vord and increases their aggression.
appearance: Tall, thin corrupted Kin with an enormously elongated mouth. No weapons. Trembles constantly.
behaviors: Stays at edges of combat.
Shrieks when player is spotted — alerts everything nearby.
Flees from melee.
Priority kill target — silencing it reduces stronghold difficulty significantly.
abilities: Alert Shriek — calls all nearby Vord to player
Buff Shriek — increases ally damage
Retreat — runs from melee

name: Vord Mender
desc: Support enemy. Heals other Vord. Slow, but a real threat when present.
appearance: Hunched, robed Kin form. Hands constantly extended with green-glowing motes between them. Face hidden under hood.
behaviors: Stays behind front-line Vord.
Heals allies within 5m every few seconds.
Priority kill — but harder to reach.
Fragile but flees when targeted directly.
abilities: Heal Pulse — restores nearby Vord HP
Tether Heal — single-target larger heal
Cleansing Mist — removes player's poison effects (unintentionally)
drops: Spirit Anchor (rare — Mender retained some compassion)

name: Vord Carrier
desc: Large beast-of-burden Vord. Carries supplies and equipment between strongholds.
appearance: Quadrupedal, broad-backed. Visible packs and gear strapped to its back. Face is a half-corrupted Kin's, expression vacant.
behaviors: Travels between strongholds in pairs.
Non-aggressive unless attacked.
Drops significant loot if defeated.
Other Vord will defend it if attacked nearby.
abilities: Kick — defensive only
Heavy Slam — when cornered
Bray Alert — calls nearby Vord on death

name: Graze
desc: Peaceful herd animal. Roams the Lowlands. The basic source of meat and hide.
appearance: Stocky four-legged grazer with thick brown fur. Long muzzle, gentle eyes, curved horns. Hooves leave clear prints in soft soil.
behaviors: Travels in herds of 4-8.
Flees if attacked or approached aggressively.
Can be tamed with Calming Pheromone or fed grain.
Plodder Cannon mount when fully bonded.

name: Cluck
desc: Small bird-like creature. Lays eggs. Common around any settled area.
appearance: Round body, short legs, fluffy feathers in mottled grey-brown. Tiny eyes, big appetite.
behaviors: Stays close to where it spawned.
Easy to catch by hand.
Lays eggs in nests if kept in Animal Pen.
Cluck calls attract more Clucks.

name: Fleecegoat
desc: Hill-dwelling small fauna. Source of wool and milk.
appearance: Sheep-goat hybrid with thick white wool and small curved horns. Bleats when curious.
behaviors: Climbs cliffs other fauna can't.
Lets player shear it for wool without killing.
Can be milked at Auto-Milker.
Aggressive only if cornered.

name: Cavebleat
desc: Underground variant of the Graze. Lives in cave systems and produces a milkier, fattier dairy.
appearance: Smaller and paler than a Graze. Thick wool replaces most fur. Eyes adapted to low light, almost luminous.
behaviors: Solitary or in pairs.
Flees deeper into caves when threatened.
Excellent milk source — Cavebleat cheese is a chef's premium.
Vulnerable to predators in caves.

name: Cavestalker
desc: Predator. Hunts other cave fauna. Will attack the player if surprised.
appearance: Long-bodied feline with elongated legs and slitted yellow eyes. Coat is mottled grey-black for cave camouflage.
behaviors: Stalks in silence until close.
Pounces from above or hidden alcoves.
Doesn't pursue if player escapes line-of-sight.
Can be tamed (very rare) into a powerful melee companion.

name: Glimmerwing
desc: Beautiful flying creature. Sky Islands' most common fauna. Source of feathers and a rare bioluminescent organ.
appearance: Bird-like, with feathers that catch the light and shift colors. Long tail-feathers. Eyes are tiny and bright.
behaviors: Roosts at high altitudes.
Flees if approached aggressively.
Can be lured with food.
Used as a courier when tamed.

name: Driftwing
desc: Large flying creature. Sky Islands' apex aerial predator.
appearance: Massive bird-like beast with leathery wings. Long beak. Eyes that watch from any height.
behaviors: Soars high, dives on small prey.
Will attack the player if engaged in air.
Hardest fauna to tame — but a Driftwing mount is the player's first True flying companion.
Bonded Driftwings carry the player through sky islands.

name: Skyserpent
desc: Apex Sky Island predator. Snake-like, flies through the air on no visible mechanism.
appearance: Long serpentine body, covered in silver scales that catch wind. Wings are vestigial — actual flight is somehow magical.
behaviors: Solitary, territorial.
Dives at the player at high speed.
Cannot be tamed.
Drops are used in elite gadgets and weapons.

name: Snowdrifter
desc: Snow-dwelling creature. Slow but provides thick pelt and deep wool.
appearance: Heavy quadruped with white shaggy coat. Stubby horns. Trundles through snow.
behaviors: Migrates in slow herds.
Easy to track in snow.
Will fight back if attacked — a powerful charge.
Bonded for cold-resistance buff to nearby player.

name: Ash Pup
desc: Friendly canine. Player's first potential companion. Lives in mountain caves.
appearance: Small, fluffy white-grey canine with bright eyes. Pups are easy to befriend with Pet Food.
behaviors: Pups follow Mother packs.
Easily bonds with player when given Pet Food.
Trained Ash Pup is a combat companion — fights small enemies.
Will not engage bosses directly but supports player.
drops: Pelt x1 (if killed — generally not recommended)

name: Spore Floater
desc: Drifting marsh creature. Almost like a living lantern. Mostly passive but bursts spores when threatened.
appearance: Round, bioluminescent organism floating slightly above marsh water. Tendrils dangle below. Glows faintly.
behaviors: Drifts on marsh winds.
Releases small spore cloud when touched.
Dies easily from any attack.
Cluster of floaters lights up marsh paths at night.

name: Bog Frog
desc: Common marsh amphibian. Source of sticky secretions used in glue traps.
appearance: Large green frog with bulging eyes. Skin glistens with sticky mucus. Long sticky tongue.
behaviors: Sits motionless on lily pads.
Hops away when approached.
Easy to catch with Net Thrower.
Edible meat (chef cuisine).

name: Cave Eel
desc: Aquatic predator. Found in marsh water and cave pools.
appearance: Long, snake-like aquatic creature. Skin is slick, dark green. Eyes glow in water.
behaviors: Lurks in deep water.
Strikes from below at swimming players.
Vulnerable when out of water.
Eel oil is the most efficient bio-fuel.

name: Honey Bee
desc: Common pollinator. Beekeeper archetype's primary resource.
appearance: Standard fluffy bee. Black-yellow stripes. Pollen on legs.
behaviors: Lives in Apiaries and wild Honey Hives.
Friendly to player wearing Beekeeper Suit.
Aggressive otherwise — swarm attacks.
Used as ammo for Bee Cannon, transport for Bee Courier Hive.

name: Thornback
desc: Aggressive Badlands predator. Pack hunter. Difficult tame, valuable mount.
appearance: Quadruped with bristling spine of bone spikes. Reptilian skin. Hooked tail.
behaviors: Hunts in packs of 3-4.
Charges at the player from concealment.
Spikes are weaponizable.
Bonded Thornback is a deadly hunting mount.

name: Plodder
desc: Slow, massive ungulate. The Badlands' equivalent of a draft animal.
appearance: Bovine giant with thick hide and slow gait. Two curved horns. Calm eyes.
behaviors: Mostly stationary, grazing.
Will defend if attacked.
Heavy load-bearing mount.
Plodder-mounted Cannon is a mid-game vehicle.

name: Rootback
desc: Smaller herd animal. Provides quality leather.
appearance: Smaller than Plodder, sleeker. Reddish-brown fur. Roots in the soil for food.
behaviors: Travels in family groups.
Flees from predators.
Drops quality leather when killed.
Can be milked for goat-milk-like product.

name: Silk Spinner
desc: Spider-like creature. Lives in caves and ruins.
appearance: Large arachnid with long legs and a glistening silken sheen. Mostly black with white markings.
behaviors: Builds webs in caves.
Ambushes from above.
Drops silk when killed.
Aggressive only when player enters its web.

name: Wren
desc: The first Kin you rescue. Quiet for most of Act 1; becomes a central figure in the story. Holds the seventh Heart Fragment inside her — the discovery of which is the moral hinge of Act 3.
appearance: Young Kin, mid-twenties. Pale, with dark hair down past her shoulders. Wears the clothes you find her in: a torn working dress, sturdy boots. Eyes deep brown, often looking down.
behaviors: Follows the player back to base in Act 1.
Speaks only at the end of Act 1, reveals the Council's plan.
Stays at the base throughout Act 2, opening up gradually.
Acts as quest-giver for several side missions.
At end of Act 3, the player discovers her secret — and must choose.
abilities: Provides recipes for early Kin tools.
Unlocks the first Spirit Gateway recipe when trust is high.
Offers food and rest at the base.
Personality: gentle, observant, traumatized.
drops: On her own death (Act 3 choice): Heart Fragment + permanent Spirit Anchor that always speaks first when the Gateway is opened.

name: Marsh Apothecary
desc: Second rescued Kin. Found in the Fungal Marshes. Was once an alchemist for the Kin Council.
appearance: Older Kin man, white hair pulled back, wears a stained apothecary's apron with many pockets. Glasses. Hands stained green from years of brewing.
behaviors: Lives at the player's base.
Operates a Chemistry Set near his bed.
Brews unique potions on request.
Gives the player the Chemistry Set recipe.
abilities: Unlocks 5 alchemist masterwork recipes.
Will accept ingredients in exchange for prepared potions.
Mutters about plants and bugs constantly.
Personality: distracted, kind, deeply curious.
drops: Death: Spirit becomes one of the first Gateway residents (after natural in-game time).

name: Vesh the Smith
desc: Third rescued Kin. Found in a Badlands forge ruin. Was a smith before the corruption.
appearance: Burly Kin woman, dark skin and braided hair. Forearms covered in burn scars. Wears a leather apron and heavy boots.
behaviors: Works at the Smith's Anvil Station at the base.
Crafts masterwork weapons on request.
Knew Wren before the fall — their reunion is emotional.
Tells stories about old smiths of the Council.
abilities: Unlocks 5 smith masterwork weapon recipes.
Will repair any item for free.
Personality: stoic, sentimental once you earn her trust.
drops: Death: Spirit unlocks legendary forge recipes.

name: Brae the Hunter
desc: Fourth rescued Kin. Found in the Frozen Peaks. Hunted the Frost Reaver before being rescued.
appearance: Slim Kin figure in heavy fur cloak. Two scars across one cheek. Carries a bone bow. Quiet, watchful.
behaviors: Goes on hunts with the player if invited.
Provides intelligence about distant strongholds.
Trains the player in tracking (unlocks Hunter's Hood crafting).
Sleeps in the Scout's Tent at the base.
abilities: Offers Hunter quests through the Bounty Board.
Unlocks 4 Hunter-archetype recipes.
Will accompany the player into difficult zones (rare).
drops: Death: Spirit unlocks tracking-related legendary tools.

name: Kor the Scholar
desc: Fifth rescued Kin. Found on a Sky Island. Reveals the truth about VORD's origin.
appearance: Elderly Kin with a long white beard and round spectacles. Wears a robe stitched with sigils. Walking stick.
behaviors: Establishes a Reading Lectern at the base.
Decodes Kin Tablets and VORD Recordings the player brings.
Reveals key story lore over multiple conversations.
Often paired with the Apothecary discussing old Kin theology.
abilities: Unlocks all Scholar archetype recipes.
Will translate any unknown text.
Personality: wise, sometimes overwhelming with information.
drops: Death: Spirit unlocks the Knowledge Crystal endgame recipe.

name: Mira the Pacifist
desc: Optional Kin rescue. Found in a hidden grove protected by tamed creatures.
appearance: Young Kin woman in plant-fiber clothes, surrounded by small animals. Smiles often. Bare feet.
behaviors: Refuses to fight. Helps player tame creatures.
Establishes the Naturalist path at the base.
Will not enter dangerous areas.
Asks the player not to kill creatures unnecessarily.
abilities: Unlocks Calming Pheromone + Naturalist's Mantle recipes.
Will tame creatures the player brings home.
Provides Friendship Tokens daily.
drops: Death: Spirit unlocks all Pacifist-path legendary items.

name: The Wanderer
desc: The first trader the player meets. Travels alone with a pack mule. Has a different stock every visit.
appearance: Lean figure in a wide-brimmed hat, dusty road clothes. Face often shadowed. Speaks softly but charges fair prices.
behaviors: Visits the base if Trade Post + Caravan Beacon are placed.
Stays for 1-2 in-game days, then leaves.
Stock changes between visits.
Sometimes carries rare ingredients no other source has.
abilities: Trades any item for any other (with markup).
Will buy player surplus.
Sometimes shares rumors about distant strongholds.

name: The Caravan Master
desc: Leads a caravan of 4-5 NPCs. Only visits if the player has high merchant relations.
appearance: Imposing figure on a covered wagon. Long coat with many hidden pockets. Goggles for sand storms.
behaviors: Visits monthly with a full caravan.
Brings bulk goods and rare materials.
Hires the player for delivery missions.
Provides discounts based on Trader's Ledger.
abilities: Sells in bulk.
Offers protection contracts.
Carries materials from distant regions.
drops: On death of any caravan member: faction loss, no more visits.

name: The Festival Trader
desc: Only visits during festivals. Carries unique cosmetics and one-time items.
appearance: Brightly dressed in colored robes, with bells on sleeves. Cheerful, loud.
behaviors: Appears only during in-game festivals.
Sells limited-time recipes.
Always at the Festival Lantern centerpiece.
Leaves at festival end.
abilities: Sells unique festival-only items.
Sells fireworks in bulk.
Carries seasonal recipes.
